s01.text: You tap your phone hundreds of times a day. Your finger never actually touches the screen.

s02.text: Under the glass is a grid of transparent electrodes, etched into the surface and invisible to you.

s03.text: Each one forms a tiny capacitor. The glass between it and your finger is an insulator, so no current crosses.

s04.text: Your finger is conductive. It bends the electric field through the glass, and the controller reads the change at every node.

s05.text: If you land between two nodes, it compares their readings and works out where you touched. The coordinate can fall anywhere.

s06.text: That is why gloves fail. Insulate the field and the grid sees nothing at all.

s07.text: The whole interface runs on an electric field you cannot feel. You were never touching anything.
